gaps.sentence: Please ___ me to water the orchids while you are here.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody to do' = cause them not to forget; 'remember' is done by yourself.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

gaps.sentence: The new timetable has ___ every commuter in the county.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' = influence; 'effect' as a verb means bring about.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: Please be ___ — the baby is sleeping.
gaps.explanation: 'Quiet' means making little or no noise; 'quite' is an adverb meaning fairly or completely.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: My brother is six foot three — he is much ___ than me.
gaps.explanation: 'Tall' is used for people's height, so the comparative is 'taller'; 'higher' is for heights above a level.
